sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Brings in the router type
sections.what: Imports the Router type from Express, so the file can name the kind of router a tool must provide. It adds nothing when the program runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the router field needs a type name from Express.

sections.name: ToolModule
sections.title: The shape every tool must follow
sections.what: Defines the three things each backend tool provides: a URL slug that must match its folder name, a readable title for logs, and an Express router holding its endpoints.
sections.why: The file comment says the collector discovers tools by this shape, so new tools need no edits to shared files.
sections.watch_out: The slug must match the folder name, and the type cannot check that.

sections.name: isToolModule
sections.title: Checking a value is a tool
sections.what: Returns yes only if the value is an object with a non-empty slug, a text title, and a router that can be called.
sections.why: Likely reason: the collector loads files it finds automatically, so it needs a check that runs at run time.
sections.watch_out: A passing check does not confirm that the slug matches the folder or that the router has any routes.

summary: Defines the required shape of a backend tool module, and a runtime check that a loaded module has that shape.
purpose: Gives every backend tool one agreed format, so the server can find it and attach its routes under its own address without editing shared files.
why: Likely reason: the file comment says new tools should not need edits to shared routing code, and one shared shape makes that possible.
how: 1. A tool folder exports one default object of this shape. 2. The collector finds and loads that object. 3. The check confirms the object has a text slug, a text title, and a callable router. 4. The collector then attaches the router under the tool's slug, as the comments describe.
inputs: Any value the collector loads from a tool folder, treated as unknown until checked.
outputs: A yes or no answer from the check. The shape itself adds no code when the program runs.
risks: A module with a wrong slug, or a router with no routes, still passes the check and gets attached.
debug: If a tool does not appear at its address, confirm its default export has slug, title, and router, that the slug matches the folder name, and check the mount messages in the server log.
